name: How long does a retail build-out take in Los Angeles if permits are already in review?

mainEntity.name: How long does a retail build-out actually take in Los Angeles once drawings are submitted, and what parts of the schedule usually slip the most?
mainEntity.text: How long does a retail build-out actually take in Los Angeles once drawings are submitted, and what parts of the schedule usually slip the most?

acceptedAnswer.text: A retail build-out in Los Angeles usually has three timing buckets: design and permit preparation, permit review, and construction. Even when a project is straightforward, the full path from lease signing to opening often runs 4 to 8 months because landlord approvals, city plan check, revisions, and inspections all add time. Once permits are issued, a typical interior retail construction phase may take 6 to 12 weeks for a standard tenant improvement, but custom millwork, special lighting, signage, and long-lead finishes can extend that timeline. The most common delays are incomplete drawings, changes during permit review, utility coordination, and waiting on final sign-offs. If opening date matters, the best approach is to lock the scope early, order long-lead items before construction starts, and build a schedule with milestone dates instead of a single completion target.
acceptedAnswer.description: A standard retail tenant improvement in Los Angeles often takes about 4 to 8 months from lease signing to opening, with construction itself commonly lasting 6 to 12 weeks after permit approval. The biggest schedule risks are permit corrections, landlord review delays, long-lead materials, and final inspection scheduling.
